claim: Run 2 KV-cache cells: long c32 already sits at 92% KV usage (32 x 8,704 tokens = 278,528 of a 300,192-token cache); c64 and c128 are past capacity, and doubling concurrency from c32 to c64 halves throughput and multiplies median first-token latency by 15.7. c64 and c128 measure overload, not capacity.
conditions: Peaks are read from 10-second vLLM log ticks ("GPU KV cache usage"), attributed to cells by arm-log start stamps (a stamp is written at cell start: next stamp minus this stamp equals duration plus about 15 s). max_running of 36 at c64/c128 is the KV-limited steady concurrency. DISCLOSURES calls c64/c128 overload; the c32 saturation is not stated there. Preemption count is not measured: vLLM does not log it at INFO and no metrics were scraped.
implication_for_a_shop: Size max concurrency from tokens in flight against the cache, not from GPU utilisation: past the cache limit you pay 2x the concurrency for half the throughput. Any tuning number taken at c32 on this workload is a near-saturated cell.
confidence: high for KV peaks and the throughput collapse; preemption itself unmeasured
